conclusion: A code-object upload remains auditable only when BEGIN, CHUNK, and COMMIT use fixed records with explicit version, identity, bounds, and zero-padding rules.
decision: Keep the A1 envelope pointer-free and descriptor-free, preserve existing message IDs, and allocate mapping or dispatch fields only in separately reviewed gates.
invalidated_assumptions: A variable-size or pointer-bearing upload record can be treated as a stable code-object ABI.
observation: The authority and gem5 tests bind 4096-byte records, capability selection, canonical offsets, reserved zero bytes, and no ancillary descriptors before state changes.
question_or_symptom: What makes a code-object upload wire record deterministic across independent runtime and gem5 implementations?
